title: October 25–26 — the returning action and the hidden half
summary: Extends the already curated October 25 SimplyPut, SimplyPutClaude, SimplyPutSol and HailMery cards with their discriminating controls, and adds OddOne's October 25 webcam hidden-half experiment. SimplyPut shows ordinary memoized action selection; Claude's route toy retains learned reaches against shared controls; Sol's active-probe cable mechanism fails its frozen/phase-off ablation; HailMery isolates action-predicted self versus cross-modal agreement in a synthetic fixture. OddOne's six-scene saved synthetic battery distinguishes spatial light leakage from continuation, auto-exposure and failed novelty extrapolation. Its live webcam footage is a demonstration, not a controlled independent novel-position recovery result. The optical and motor branches meet only at the methodological question: can return signals reveal what is hidden without mistaking priors for observations?

nodes.claim: Online webcam hidden-half predictor: a CPU linear Wiener/ridge lens and an optional CNN predict changes in one half of the image from the other. It includes frozen-test diagnostics, brightness/time-shuffle controls, a synthetic corner-light battery and singular-value experiments.
nodes.survived: Saved six-scene synthetic diagnosis separates coarse light and shadow readout from independent halves: at 1/8 resolution R² is 0.55 for glow, 0.728 for edge shadow and -0.074 for independent input. The edge case beats glow; the full-resolution gain is smaller (0.131 versus 0.052). A separate idealized singular-value fixture shows why an occluding edge can increase resolvable channels. The code also provides live webcam display, train/freeze, score and channel analysis.
nodes.killed: Near-perfect synthetic crosser R²=0.963 at full resolution is primarily object continuation across the split; exposure R²=0.985 matches a brightness-only baseline. A novel-colour test collapses to R²=-10.516 at full resolution. Novelty cutoff was revised after seeing the test, and no frozen, independently audited live-camera test establishes that previously unseen positions are physically reconstructed rather than extrapolated. Frame-by-frame prequential scoring alone does not remove temporal dependence.
nodes.era: October 25–26: visible evidence versus learned guesses

edges.why: SimplyPutClaude explicitly names the simpler context-keyed bell memory as its sibling control, then tackles retention under sequential learning in a shared arm controller, not a direct code fork.

SimplyPutSol explicitly names Claude's route-controller test and changes the learning interface from corrective joint-angle error to scalar feedback from the learner's own randomized probes. The mechanism ablation fails, unlike the route toy's retention gate.
OddOne's README explicitly calls the webcam experiment a cousin of Varjoluotain's light-transport inverse-periscopy problem, without copying its occluder model.

OddOne explicitly refers to KulmanTakaa as the corner-camera relative. Unlike the early browser instrument's proposed hidden-actor bench, OddOne provides a split-webcam lens and measured synthetic optical-leak controls.

Both ask whether observed image context can constrain missing image content. DoDis retrieves donor residues; OddOne learns a visible-to-hidden predictive channel. This is conceptual comparison, not inheritance or a claim that image plausibility proves optical visibility.

motifs.title: A learned action is not the same claim as a learned cable
motifs.description: A small action table and memoized shortcut succeed at repeated known targets; experience-assigned expert routes protect sequential reaches in a supervised synthetic arm; paired physical-style probes do not yet beat fixed cables or solve forgetting. Compare causal controls before attributing a skill to tissue-like dynamics.

motifs.title: The self-model test must contain the system's own actions
motifs.description: In HailMery's synthetic mirror fixture, correlated sensory streams describe both self and imitator. Conditioning on one's motor history separates components over a finite timing window; the proposed observer-of-observers and consciousness interpretation remain untested.

motifs.title: The hidden scene is recoverable only where a measurable channel carries it
motifs.description: Visible shadows and low-frequency illumination can constrain hidden motion, but across-boundary continuation, camera auto-exposure and prior-driven completions can mimic sight. OddOne reports synthetic discriminators; fresh live-camera optical interventions remain the decisive missing test.
